title: $50,000 Car Loan Payment: 48, 60 & 72 Months (2026)
metaDescription: A $50,000 car loan costs $990.06/mo at 7% APR over 60 months. Compare 48/60/72-month payments at 5–9%, total interest, and depreciation risk.

hero.lede: Monthly payments on $50,000 of auto financing across 5%–9% APRs and 48/60/72-month terms, plus total interest and what depreciation does to your equity along the way.

shortAnswer.heading: What does a $50,000 car loan cost per month?
shortAnswer.html: A $50,000 car loan costs about $990.06 a month at 7% APR over 60 months, with $9,404 of total interest. On 48 months the payment is $1,197.31 ($7,471 interest); on 72 months it's $852.45 ($11,376 interest). Your APR and down payment move these numbers — the tables below cover 5%–9%.

sections.title: Payment vs. interest: the term is the real decision.
paragraphs: A $50,000 car loan at 7% runs $990.06 per month on a 60-month term, with $9,404 of lifetime interest. The term is the big trade-off: 48 months means $1,197.31/month but only $7,471 of interest, while 72 months lowers the payment to $852.45 at a cost of $11,376 in interest.

sections.title: Total interest on $50,000 over the loan.
sections.note: At 7%, choosing 72 months over 48 costs $3,906 more in interest on this loan — the price of the lower monthly payment.

sections.title: The car loses value faster than the loan pays down.
paragraphs: Cars depreciate faster than long loans amortize. A typical new vehicle loses about 20% of its value in year one and roughly 15% a year after that — so a $50,000 car is worth around $34,000 after two years. On a 72-month loan at 7% you'd still owe about $35,599 at that point — roughly $1,599 of negative equity. Shorter terms and bigger down payments keep the balance under the car's value.

faq.q: What is the monthly payment on a $50,000 car loan?
faq.a: At 7% APR, a $50,000 car loan costs $990.06 a month over 60 months, $1,197.31 over 48 months, or $852.45 over 72 months. Across the 5%–9% APR range, the 60-month payment runs $943.56–$1,037.92.

faq.q: How much interest will I pay on a $50,000 auto loan?
faq.a: At 7% APR, total interest is $7,471 over 48 months, $9,404 over 60, and $11,376 over 72. The longer the term, the lower the payment but the higher the total cost — 72 months costs $3,906 more than 48 at the same rate.

faq.q: Is a 72-month loan a bad idea for $50,000?
faq.a: Not automatically, but it has two costs: $3,906 more interest than a 48-month term at 7%, and a longer stretch of negative equity — around month 24 you'd owe about $35,599 while a typical $50,000 car is worth roughly $34,000. If you need 72 months to afford the payment, consider a cheaper car or a larger down payment.

faq.q: What credit score do I need for a good rate on $50,000?
faq.a: The 5%–9% range shown spans roughly prime to near-prime pricing in 2026; top-tier borrowers on new cars can beat it, while subprime rates run well above it. On this loan, each 1% of APR changes the 60-month payment by about $23.76/month — so improving your score before buying has a measurable payoff.

faq.q: Should I put money down on a $50,000 car?
faq.a: Yes, if you can — every $1,000 of down payment cuts the 60-month payment at 7% by about $19.80/month and reduces the risk of owing more than the car is worth. A 10–20% down payment typically keeps the balance below the depreciation curve from day one.

methodology: Payments use the standard amortization formula with monthly compounding on $50,000 financed. APRs shown (5%–9%) are illustrative steps spanning typical 2026 prime/near-prime pricing, not offers.

Depreciation figures use a typical curve — about 20% loss in year one and 15% per year thereafter — applied to the financed amount as a proxy for vehicle price with zero down. Individual models vary widely.
Figures exclude sales tax, title/registration fees, dealer add-ons, and insurance. Educational estimates — not lending or financial advice.
